shared_text:
The flight. A narrow-body airliner on a satellite-guided (RNAV RNP) approach to an airport in the morning, in visual conditions.

The crew. The captain was the pilot flying and the first officer the pilot monitoring. The first officer had about 160 hours on type, all in the last 90 days. Neither pilot had flown into the airport before; both had studied the company's airport pages and guide.

What happened. On the arrival the aircraft was cleared to a fix at 12,000 ft and 230 knots. As briefed, the crew used half speed brakes from that fix. Cleared for the approach, they armed it and set 6,500 ft in the altitude window. The flight mode annunciators showed speed and final approach modes. The aircraft levelled briefly at 10,600 ft between two fixes, then began the approach descent with half speed brakes still out and accelerated to 260 knots. Unable to slow to landing gear speed, the captain disconnected the autopilot and selected full speed brakes. The descent rate was reduced and the speed came back; at 230 knots the gear was lowered, then flaps 1 and 2 on schedule. The aircraft crossed the next fix at 6,500 ft, hand-flown, with gear down, flaps 2 and 190 knots. It then descended below 6,500 ft, a 'sink rate' alert sounded, and the aircraft reached 6,200 ft. The tower called the crew to check their altitude. The crew stopped the descent by hand and climbed back to 6,500 ft.
safe_outcome: The autopilot was re-engaged, managed speed was selected, and flaps 3 and then full were set on schedule. The aircraft was stabilised on the approach profile at 1,200 ft above the ground, and the rest of the approach and the landing were uneventful. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was crossing nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.

Moved under rule 5: re-engaging the autopilot, the final configuration, being stabilised at 1,200 ft above the ground, and the landing. Removed under rule 6: the airport, runway number, arrival and fix names, and the approach letter. Judgement calls: (1) the only reporter is the first officer as pilot monitoring, so the captain is taken as pilot flying ('autopilot was disengaged by pilot flying'); the captain's experience is not given; (2) the first officer's 161.57 hours on type equals the 90-day figure, written as 'about 160 hours on type, all in the last 90 days'; (3) 'in the morning' comes from the coded local-time band; (4) 'brick and blue stick' (vertical guidance symbols) is left out as jargon whose meaning is not certain; the flight mode annunciator modes are kept; (5) 'cleaned the RNAV RNP Z' is read as 'cleared'. Bracket: 'crossing', because the aircraft descended about 300 ft below the fix altitude on the approach near a Class D airport, where the plausible conflict is lower traffic crossing the approach path. No traffic interaction in the report, so the standard safe-ending sentences are used.
